page: Google Cloud Platform m1-ultramem-80 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance engineered for workloads demanding an exceptionally high memory-to-vCPU ratio. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the system is powered by dedicated Intel Xeon processors running at a base clock speed of 2.2 GHz across 40 physical cores and 80 vCPUs. The hardware configuration integrates 55 MB of L3 cache, 32 KB of L1d cache, and 0.25 MB of L2 cache per core. The central highlight of the configuration is its massive 1922.0 GB memory footprint, offering approximately 24.02 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance includes no bundled local storage and provides zero discrete graphics processors or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark measurements indicate a pronounced divergence between single-threaded and parallel execution. Single-core performance ranks in the lowest tier, reflected by a stress-ng single-core score of 847.69, a Geekbench single-core score of 849.0, and low throughput in single-threaded gzip compression at 19.68 GB/sec. Conversely, multi-threaded throughput achieves balanced, mid-tier results across standard suites, marked by a stress-ng multi-core result of 40217.38, a Geekbench multi-core score of 8396.0, and a Passmark CPU score of 39241.27. Memory subsystem performance demonstrates 123.42 GB/sec in uncached read bandwidth and 58.75 GB/sec in write bandwidth, enabling the platform to sustain 40.16 million Redis SET operations per second.

From an infrastructure and cost perspective, the instance is specialized for density in system RAM rather than raw compute velocity. The 2.2 GHz processor architecture without AVX-512 capabilities presents a throughput tradeoff for compute-bound algorithms, meaning resource investment is heavily skewed toward memory allocation. Consequently, the m1-ultramem-80 is best suited for large-scale in-memory databases such as SAP HANA, massive Redis or Memcached clusters, enterprise caching layers, and high-footprint extract-transform-load (ETL) pipelines.
